title: Descent of etale-local universal coequalizers with finite etale targets
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme, let $a,b:Z\rightrightarrows P$ be morphisms of $Y$-schemes, and let $(u_i:U_i\to Y)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed family of etale morphisms whose images cover $Y$. For a $Y$-scheme $T$ and $V\to Y$ write $T_V=T\times_YV$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose that for each $i$ there are a finite etale $U_i$-scheme $Q_i$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] and a $U_i$-morphism $q_i:P_{U_i}\to Q_i$ with $q_i\circ a_{U_i}=q_i\circ b_{U_i}$. For a $U_i$-scheme $W$ and a morphism $V\to U_i$ write $W_V=W\times_{U_i}V$; thus $P_V=P\times_YV=(P_{U_i})_V$, $a_V,b_V$ are the base changes of $a_{U_i},b_{U_i}$, and $(q_i)_V=q_i\times_{U_i}V:P_V\to(Q_i)_V$. Assume the following universal property: for every $V\to U_i$, every $V$-scheme $H$, and every $V$-morphism $h:P_V\to H$ satisfying $h\circ a_V=h\circ b_V$, there is exactly one $V$-morphism $k:(Q_i)_V\to H$ with $k\circ(q_i)_V=h$.
Then there are a finite etale $Y$-scheme $Q$ and a $Y$-morphism $q:P\to Q$ with $q\circ a=q\circ b$, and isomorphisms of $U_i$-schemes $\theta_i:Q_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_i$ with $\theta_i\circ q_{U_i}=q_i$. Moreover, for every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$, every $Y'$-scheme $H$, and every $Y'$-morphism $h:P_{Y'}\to H$ with $h\circ a_{Y'}=h\circ b_{Y'}$, there is exactly one $Y'$-morphism $k:Q_{Y'}\to H$ with $k\circ q_{Y'}=h$. Neither $P$ nor $Z$ is assumed finite etale; only the local quotient targets $Q_i$ are.

proof.text: We will use representable-sheaf gluing in the following precise form. If $(B_i\to B)$ is an etale cover and $X,H$ are arbitrary $B$-schemes, then compatible $B_i$-maps $X_{B_i}\to H_{B_i}$ glue uniquely to a $B$-map $X\to H$. Indeed $(X_{B_i}\to X)$ is an etale cover by covering base change. Apply the representable-sheaf lemma on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ to the $X$-scheme $X\times_BH$: its sections on $X_{B_i}$ are exactly these maps, by the fibre-product universal property. The uniqueness assertion also detects equality of two $B$-maps after this cover.

Put $U_{ij}=U_i\times_YU_j$. Over $U_{ij}$ the pullbacks $q_i^{ij}$ and $q_j^{ij}$ are coequalizers of the same pair, by the stated universal properties with $V=U_{ij}$. Applying the first to $h=q_j^{ij}$ gives a unique $\varphi_{ij}:(Q_i)_{U_{ij}}\to(Q_j)_{U_{ij}}$ with $\varphi_{ij}q_i^{ij}=q_j^{ij}$. Reversing $i,j$ gives its inverse: both inverse composites and the identities have the same composite with the appropriate quotient map, so uniqueness makes them equal. This construction pulls back to every $W\to U_{ij}$, since the pulled-back comparison still satisfies the defining equation and both pulled-back quotient maps still have the assumed universal property. On $U_i\times_YU_j\times_YU_k$, the maps $\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}$ and $\varphi_{ik}$ therefore both compose with $q_i$ to $q_k$; uniqueness gives the cocycle equation.

proof.text: Form $U=\coprod_iU_i$ and $R=\coprod_iQ_i$, with their induced maps $u:U\to Y$ and $r:R\to U$. The coproduct lemma gives pairwise disjoint open-and-closed summands covering each scheme. Each $Q_i\to R\to U$ is the finite etale structure map $Q_i\to U_i$ followed by the open immersion $U_i\to U$, hence is etale by composition and the open-immersion case. Source locality gives that $r$ is etale, and similarly that $u$ is etale. On the target open $U_i$ the restriction of $r$ is exactly $Q_i\to U_i$: its inverse image consists of the $i$th summand, since every other summand maps to a disjoint $U_j$. Target locality of finiteness thus makes $r$ finite. The map $u$ is surjective because the original family covers $Y$. In particular $R$ is finite etale over $U$. Pulling the summand open coverings back preserves open immersions and coverings; the fibre-product universal property identifies the resulting pieces of $U\times_YU$ and of $U\times_YU\times_YU$ with $U_{ij}$ and $U_i\times_YU_j\times_YU_k$, respectively.

proof.text: Let $p_1,p_2:U\times_YU\to U$. On the component $U_{ij}$ the two pullbacks $p_1^*R,p_2^*R$ restrict to $(Q_i)_{U_{ij}},(Q_j)_{U_{ij}}$. These components are open immersions into $U\times_YU$ (step 3), hence etale by the open-immersion case of the composition lemma, and they cover it; so they form an etale cover. Use step 1 for this disjoint open covering by the components to glue the maps $\varphi_{ij}$ to a map $\varphi:p_1^*R\to p_2^*R$; the inverse maps glue too and their composites are identities by the equality part of step 1. On the triple product the cocycle equality holds on every component by step 2, hence globally by step 1. Thus $(R,\varphi)$ is a finite etale descent datum for the surjective etale morphism $u$, in the stated definition. Apply the equivalence of finite etale descent to obtain a finite etale $Y$-scheme $Q$ and a datum-compatible isomorphism $\psi:Q_U\xrightarrow{\sim}R$. Its restrictions give $\theta_i:Q_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_i$, with $\varphi_{ij}(\theta_i)_{U_{ij}}=(\theta_j)_{U_{ij}}$ under the canonical pullback identifications.

proof.text: The $U_i$-maps $\theta_i^{-1}q_i:P_{U_i}\to Q_{U_i}$ agree on overlaps: after composing the $i$th map with $(\theta_j)_{U_{ij}}=\varphi_{ij}(\theta_i)_{U_{ij}}$, its value is $\varphi_{ij}q_i^{ij}=q_j^{ij}$. Step 1 with $X=P,H=Q,B=Y$ therefore glues them uniquely to $q:P\to Q$. The equation $\theta_iq_{U_i}=q_i$ holds by construction. Since the $q_i$ equalize the local arrows, $(qa)_{U_i}=(qb)_{U_i}$ for all $i$. The equality part of step 1, now with $X=Z,H=Q$, gives $qa=qb$. Neither use of gluing asks that $P$ or $Z$ be etale.

Fix $Y'\to Y$, a $Y'$-scheme $H$ and an equalizing map $h:P_{Y'}\to H$. Put $W_i=Y'\times_YU_i$; these form an etale cover of $Y'$. The original universal property, applied to $W_i\to U_i$ and $h_{W_i}$, gives a unique map $(Q_i)_{W_i}\to H_{W_i}$ factoring $h_{W_i}$. Composing with the pulled-back $\theta_i$ gives $k_i:Q_{W_i}\to H_{W_i}$ with $k_iq_{W_i}=h_{W_i}$. On $W_i\times_{Y'}W_j$, the restrictions of $k_i,k_j$ agree: both have composite $h$ with $q$, and the original universal property for $q_i$ over that overlap, transported by $\theta_i$, says there is exactly one such map. Step 1 with $B=Y',X=Q_{Y'},H=H$ glues the $k_i$ to $k:Q_{Y'}\to H$. Checking on the cover of $P_{Y'}$ gives $kq_{Y'}=h$. Any other factor has restriction $k_i$ by local uniqueness, hence equals $k$ by the equality assertion of step 1 on $Q_{Y'}$. This proves the universal property for every $Y'\to Y$.
